source: existing films and stills, nothing re-rendered

01 title: a goal-conditioned diffusion policy for robotic drawing,
a simulated pen plotter, and the ink it actually laid down
02 finished page: four cameras, one sheet, ink painted onto the paper
03 the goal: a 48 x 48 picture of a cat
no stroke names, no oracle ordering, no target path
04 reverse diffusion: one picture in, one 512-point pen program out
ink F1 0.395 to 0.794, ink on the page 268.2 units to 15.25
05 the path: x, y and a pen carried at plus or minus one,
so one noise scale fits all three channels
05 the path scored: rasterised back to a picture and scored against its goal
ink F1 0.729, 19 of 23 strokes, pen agreement 0.748
06 the machine: a MuJoCo gantry plotter, 33 substeps per 60 Hz frame,
07 the policy's program: the same planner, the same machine, the same camera gates
worst stroke registration 4.38 px, centroid 6.3 px
09 checkpoint: epoch 10: val loss 0.091, ink F1 0.310, 4.9 strokes
epoch 120: val loss 0.229, ink F1 0.732, 20.2 strokes
the shipping choice was made on the drawing, not the loss
10 limitations: no closed loop: the program is sampled once and run open loop
no physical plotter: dynamics, contact and camera are simulated
one cat in many styles, and no cross-category claim
11 closing: is in a log under out/, and src/verify.py fails the build
